notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game, September 2025
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome to the September Exo Rally update![/h1][p][/p][p]We've been hard at work finishing one of the last (?) planets, Fusang, a volcano world. The current planet list now includes:[/p][p]- Dhool (meteor desert world)[/p][p]- Lunar (Earth's moon)[/p][p]- Tensei (strip mined, earth quake riddled planet)[/p][p]- New Earth (terraformed forest planet)[/p][p]- Fusang (volcano world)

Hopefully we will still have time to add one last planet, but 5 is a decent start point at least for release.[/p][p][/p][h1]Fusang - Volcano World[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/5208b8e7db8a4bcadd36390f31bb434982540d24.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Fusang is a tidally locked planet close to a binary star system, which causes a large heat gradient from the hot to the cold side, as well as extreme volcanism. It is on the more difficult end of the spectrum in Exo Rally, and features a much bumpier surface, lava river canyons, unexpected drop offs and an array of hazards. Careful speed management is more important here than anywhere else on the rally circuit.[/p][h2]Lava Bombs[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/5c81cd0d03c1884599eb3a6a9c8fd768d80ca267.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Most of the volcanos in Fusang eject lava bombs that fall and roll down across the stage area - they create moving obstacles and once they stop rolling, stationary ones as well. They can be tricky as they bounce off terrain and other boulders, and sometimes are hard to see coming. Luckily your rover is fairly tough, and direct impacts typically don't cause much more than a tire or wheel failure. [/p][p]The rule for Fusang, we feel, will be - always take 3 spare wheels![/p][p]We will be looking at your feedback if you're a tester to see what you think of this planetary feature![/p][h2]Lava Rivers[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/b55b8d30b8998b353c88967f25b675b28b7942f0.png"][/img][/p][p]Highly viscous lava rivers cover large areas, and are a threat to both your tires and RCS fuel. Driving directly over and on top of lava causes your tires to rapidly heat up to the point they'll catch fire and begin melting, however brief crossings are quite safe as your rover's high tech rubber tires don't conduct heat. Care must be taken to limit wheel spin on lava as this will rapidly increase heat, and sink the tire into the lava.[/p][p]At around 1200C, lava will also quickly cook your RCS fuel and cause it to cook off on individual thrusters and even eventually ignite your fuel tanks, so keep an eye on your temperatures.[/p][h2]Lava Fountains[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8c37d3e2e5352f0d61b1a34966ece909bcb4b775.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Volcanic vents eject lava out in fountains that can drop onto your rover and cause damage to any and all of your rovers systems. The close you get to the center of a fountain, the more damage and the quicker you'll receive damage to your systems as lava melts through your systems, damages suspension and punctures tires.[/p][p][/p][h2]Fire Tornados[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/cdfd4ff8fc22e7e8b24006749480c5e27481ec77.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As hot air travels from the hot to the dark side, high speed air currents form tornados that pickup hot gasses and lava that ignite to form fire tornados. In addition to high speed shrapnel damage, fire tornados will also quickly overheat your rover's RCS systems.[/p][p][/p][h1]Heavier Rovers, Lighter Fuel[/h1][p]From both playing Exo Rally now for years, and also watching both new and old players, I became increasingly annoyed with the tendency for rovers, especially the 6-wheeled Exo6, to 'kick' the rear up over bumps. While you'd possibly expect racing vehicles to be better the lighter their weight, current-day off-road racing trucks like Trophy Trucks actually have a sweet spot which is quite heavy, that keeps them more level over bumpy terrain due to inertia and weight resisting rotation. Given our rovers have to tackle terrain even bumpier than stuff in Baja or Dakar, we've pushed the rovers weight up quite a bit, and also reduced fuel weight at the same time for a couple of reasons:[/p][list][*][p]Lighter fuel means one setup feels more similar between min and max fuel loads, and we can stay more stable in both situations[/p][/*][*][p]After introducing RCS overheating, choosing different fuel loads became less important, as you usually couldn't use it all up in one stage[/p][/*][*][p]A more stable weight gives each rover class a more defined feel and character (a heavy rover wont feel like a lighter one on lower fuel loads)[/p][/*][/list][p]So the TLDR is that rovers now fly much straighter and flatter over most (not all!) terrain. You'll still hit bumps and jumps with just the wrong shape at just the wrong speed and get some big kicks, but it shouldn't be a near constant RCS correction required as it once was for many bumps.[/p][p][/p][h2]Screenshot mode[/h2][p]For those who love dialing in some nicely framed photos, you can now pause at any time, or during replay to save a screenshot to Steam.[/p][p]Controls include:[/p][list][*][p]Tilt/dutch[/p][/*][*][p]Fstop[/p][/*][*][p]Focal Length[/p][/*][*][p]Focus offset[/p][/*][*][p]FOV[/p][/*][*][p]Orbit/look direction/pan/dolly[/p][/*][/list][p]Here's a few![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/e3b5c66d1155de6d9803aa834bc8308ac7c22e7a.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/0fed71f7fca469d647621dc042396743fb360297.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/d8d40242693bf61865e9a559fdee55d8a2594f79.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/c14b0acd56c4fa7e49e7e7258c90f5369457e190.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Sept 2025 Update [/h1][p]Playtesters, please read the FULL release notes below before posting bugs/thoughts/feedback, thank you! [/p][list][*][p]Fusang, volcanic planet complete[/p][/*][*][p]Fusang: Lava that melts tires, fire tornados, lava fountains, rolling lava bombs, steam obstacles[/p][/*][*][p]Fusang: Ash fall weather that coats the surface in ash (reduced traction/increased drag)[/p][/*][*][p]Rovers made heavier to increase stability and fly flatter over most jumps and bumps[/p][/*][*][p]Fuel weight greatly reduced, so a setup will work better between min and max fuel[/p][/*][*][p]Tire model tweaks[/p][/*][*][p]Pace note update + linked close notes together along with a ! to draw attention[/p][/*][*][p]Mining rover is now more of a 'fixed suspension distance' vehicle (minimal travel)[/p][/*][*][p]Photo mode, drone or orbit with aperture/fov/dutch(tilt)/focal length/focus offset[/p][/*][*][p]Volumetric headlight dust[/p][/*][*][p]Headlight shadows added[/p][/*][*][p]Update to sand-like ground material physics (more consistent)[/p][/*][*][p]Improved blending between checkpoint light walls and other fx/distant light walls[/p][/*][*][p]Monoliths now interfere with the HUD/comms[/p][/*][*][p]Tensei lighting minor improvement[/p][/*][*][p]New Earth, more details and different ground materials, slightly less grass[/p][/*][*][p]Map wide stages on Fusang only (for now) with extremely long distances between checkpoints[/p][/*][*][p]Rain updates to all planets[/p][/*][*][p]Rover setup screen, some sliders faster to move[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed drone's spotlight being rotated incorrectly[/p][/*][*][p]Added dust build up to all rovers[/p][/*][*][p]Improved reflections (may be too much reflection on some ground materials in non-wet weather still)[/p][/*][*][p]Tread loss now controlled per ground material (less loss on stuff like sand, more on rock)[/p][/*][*][p]Damage to suspension now only occurs vertically if fully compressed[/p][/*][*][p]New stage overview music[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed collider on Tensei 'snow-trees'[/p][/*][*][p]Crosses visible on the checkpoint lightwalls earlier now[/p][/*][*][p]Headlight improvements/should look better against particle effects[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed: Ambient intensity increasing each time a planet is restarted[/p][/*][*][p]Updated service UI repair tabs[/p][/*][*][p]Removed eye-level bar from Exo4[/p][/*][*][p]Tornados no longer 'get you' after crossing the finish line, and dissipate near some terrain types/objects[/p][/*][*][p]Fix: rear wheels always account for toe correctly now[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced excessive wheel skew on impacts[/p][/*][*][p]Fix: replay camera skipping static cameras[/p][/*][*][p]Smoothed out camera-look which should help over smaller bumps and whoops[/p][/*][*][p]Minor strength boost to rcs-steer[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced size of checkpoint spheres to prevent wheels being ripped off occasionally[/p][/*][*][p]Donuts now require 340 deg to complete compared to 300 previously (may vary for custom checkpoint sequences)[/p][/*][*][p]Rover setup saving: now auto focuses[/p][/*][*][p]Fix: rcs fuel not being consumed at slight inputs[/p][/*][*][p]Fix: saving spare tires in tunings[/p][/*][*][p]New Earth should be less blinding[/p][/*][*][p]RCS override timer increased[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced FPP camera shake values[/p][/*][/list][p] WIP (might be broken): [/p][list][*][p]New tutorials[/p][/*][*][p]Team comms appear when starting your first event/series[/p][/*][/list][p] Known: [/p][list][*][p]Photo mode doesn't highlight some controls[/p][/*][*][p]Exo4 might be particularly hard to flip with RCS with certain setup configs[/p][/*][*][p]NPCs still think you're still on Dhool when on other planets[/p][/*][*][p]Trainings are in progress, so may not work as expected[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game, June 2025
notes.content: [h1]Welcome to the June Exo Rally update![/h1][p][/p][p]Since it's been a little while, it's a big one! The current planet list now includes:[/p][p]- Dhool (meteor desert world)[/p][p]- Lunar (Earth's moon)[/p][p]- Tensei (strip mined, earth quake riddled planet)[/p][p]- New Earth (terraformed forest planet)[/p][p][/p][p]...and we've recently begun work on a deadly volcanic world, "Fusang". Here's a look at both:[/p][p][/p][h1]New Earth[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/ed749c06adc367596deee9b66ee85c23c09b7aa0.png"][/img][/p][p]New Earth was seeded with trees and grasses from earth over the course of 100's of years, creating a green, earth-like forest-world.[/p][p][/p][p]This planet is somewhat easy to drive with plains and rolling hills, but of course with densely wooded areas, destruction is always close at hand! Terraforming structures still dot the landscape, emitting gas that is still helping to fine tune the atmosphere - it creates dense blankets of cloud that completely block visibility. If in doubt, flat out?[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="vxzRO0hwlag;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1]Fusang[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/7a25dac515805de69b977993bf6400fe8ce4ae78.png"][/img][/p][p]Fusang, a tidally locked planet in a system orbiting a nearby black hole, features a raft of deadly challenges, including tire-melting lava, fuel-igniting temperatures, fire tornadoes, lava fountains and more. [/p][p][/p][p]Even today's tires can manage a brief skip over lava, due to rubbers low thermal conductivity, but in the near future of Exo Rally, drivers can push the limits by 10s of seconds before their tires pick up molten clinkers, catch fire and finally explode. It's just wise not to spin your wheels and really dig into the molten surface...[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/b55b8d30b8998b353c88967f25b675b28b7942f0.png"][/img][/p][p]In the furnaces of open volcanos and whirling fire tornados, your tires can melt, rover's systems can cook and ignite your RCS fuel tanks if you stay too long, or push your RCS heat levels so high they're unusable.[/p][p][/p][p]If your rover takes too many showers in lava fountains, it'll collect more and more molten rock, weighing you down, sticking to tires and jamming up suspension. [/p][p][/p][p]And like Tensei, Fusang is also visited by earthquakes as a nearby black hole pulls on the planet.[/p][p][/p][p]Finally, you'll have to dodge incoming lava bombs ejected from numerous volcanoes dotted across the landscape. GL, HF![/p][p][/p][h1]Tornadoes[/h1][p]We've added tornadoes to Dhool's storm weathers, and also Fusang in a fire variant. In the outer radius, your rover is showered with shrapnel that can puncture tires and vital systems. And of course the closer you get, the more your rover is pulled around before being lifted off up into the funnel entirely.[/p][p][/p][p]Tornadoes move across the surface as well, so you'll need to adjust your racing line to steer clear.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="WnuKK4mlMYQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1]New Suspension: Dual Rate Springs and Bypass Shocks[/h1][p]Players familiar with current day off-road racing or simulations might already be familiar with the new, super customizable dual-rate springs and 6-stage bypass shocks that allow players to adjust spring strengths and dampers by compression distance and speed, both bump and rebound.[/p][p][/p][h1]RCS Changes[/h1][p]We've added a power sweet spot, where >50% heat level will gain you additional thruster strength. Power was slightly reduced below this threshold. We've also got per planet heat baselines and heat up/cool down rates, which for example means that the Moon has a low baseline, but very slow cooldown due to lack of atmosphere. Thrusters will now more realistically shed heat faster at high temps, and glow as they heat up.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/e603c6cf9467056b8ab34698e44ddffa2fdd78f8.png"][/img][/p][p]We've added detailed overheating mechanics, including the ability to cancel automatic RCS shutdown. Once you reach > 100% heat, your RCS will take more and more damage effects like melting, fuel leaks, jams, thruster explosions and finally catastrophic fuel tank explosion. So while a strategic and brief override into >100% heat levels occasionally is ok, if you really push it you'll regret it![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/a3800052ba5f33d15ac88c39405aeb17d3282fa2.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/3ef2566112c25840dd3243bb5a1e3a63e5104543.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]New Daily Stages[/h1][p]We'll be launching with the following events:[/p][p]- Daily A (random class/planet)[/p][p]- Daily B (random class/planet)[/p][p]- Weekly (random class/planet)[/p][p]- Ironman (one attempt only)[/p][p]- New "[b]Oblivion[/b]" type. For those that thought Ironman was too easy, in this mode, you'll have one attempt only with no droning, no stage overview, cockpit view only, limited RCS fuel and no spare tires.[/p][p][/p][h1]The somewhat full list![/h1][list][*][p]Physics optimizations: frame rate (accuracy) around 4x'd for around the same performance, should help with damage consistency. Playtesters, please let us know if you notice any degraded feeling from handling or frame rate problems.[/p][/*][*][p]Some performance improvements on CPU and GPU[/p][/*][*][p]New damage detection system to go with above. Damage may currently be a bit too high, but should feel consistent. [/p][/*][*][p]New suspension system, dual rate springs, 6 stage bypass dampers[/p][/*][*][p]Initial rover setups for above, some might need more tuning than others[/p][/*][*][p]New 'testing' sliders for suspension[/p][/*][*][p]Added downward force to rover test-drops on service screen, not just height as it was before (needs tweaking!)[/p][/*][*][p]Tuning sliders rounded up/dn[/p][/*][*][p]Old style 'terrain scanner' partially back in (only shows drop offs, the main 'impossible to see' terrain)[/p][/*][*][p]New planet, New Earth, terraformed forest world[/p][/*][*][p]New Dailies: Daily A, B, Weekly (all classes). New type (Oblivion)[/p][/*][*][p]Oblivion: Ironman-like with no droning, no stage overview, cockpit view only, no spare tires.[/p][/*][*][p]Tornados in Dhool's storm weather[/p][/*][*][p]RCS heat changes: 'power sweet spot' >50% heat. Per planet heat baselines and heat up/cool down rates.[/p][/*][*][p]RCS overheat damage: thrusters melt/rotate/get blocked/explode etc[/p][/*][*][p]RCS heat shutdown override: engage before or after overheating to risk damage to RCS but maintain control. D-Pad Up, Up.[/p][/*][*][p]RCS repairs added for above[/p][/*][*][p]RCS thrusters glow when reaching critical heat levels[/p][/*][*][p]Lunar RCS heat: due to lack of atmosphere, cooling is severely reduced, but starting temps are lower.[/p][/*][*][p]Checkpoint light wall brightness method change (let us know if any too dim or bright)[/p][/*][*][p]Hopefully improved transparency handling with light walls and other transparent particles/fx[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked chassis colliders on mining and rover classes (let us know if any bad looking collisions),[/p][/*][*][p]Credits screen added[/p][/*][*][p]Dust storm weather particles not completely opaque anymore[/p][/*][/list][p]While we were aiming for mid this year for release, some unexpected personal issues have come up that have made that a bit too ambitious right now. Q4 is now looking more likely.[/p]

notes.title: Exo Rally, 2nd Playtest Underway
notes.content:
Happy to announce development is proceeding well and we’re targeting mid this year for full release. 

If you’re a playtester, we have a new build now live for you to try! We're not yet decided on whether we will be adding more testers at this point.

This is a fairly unstable, early stage, unbalanced build so please don't have super high expectations. There's a bunch of unfinished stuff in here! Would love your feedback on what is working, though!

[h1]PLANETS[/h1]

[b]Lunar[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/e1356276b5ac632d9e4f2d9bc727e1169979966d.jpg[/img]
This is a very, very low gravity body so traction is almost non-existent. It's a completely different driving feel, and requires copious RCS usage to stay grounded/upright.

[b]Tensei[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/7cdb214627017f6dc06e867f38be87448d81b684.jpg[/img]
A 0.8x earth-gravity world, once a mining planet, now abandoned and eroding away over time. Extensive over-mining has caused constant planet-wide earthquakes, and these will cause traction challenges while racing. Due to the low temperatures, some ice lakes and rivers have formed on the surface and present more traction challenges.

Tensei is currently a one-stage hill climb event (Tensei's Peak) that runs approximately 20 minutes from the coast to the peak. More hand made and/or random stages probably to come.

Earthquakes are detected by your rover's seismograph part, and give you 3 seconds to respond to the incoming quake.

[b]Dhool[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/af5482cd6621b527c3852d8b56db9a04c0a485fc.png[/img]
Go check this out in the demo now if you're yet to try the game! A challenging meteor wracked desert world with earth-like gravity and atmosphere.


[h1]CLASSES[/h1]

[b]UTV[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/c6ae5715469ee82eff65a3ab24a4c943b01ce34c.png[/img]
A lightweight, front-biased 4WD with 250HP. Primary power goes to the front axle, giving the rover a somewhat FF feel, but with the highly necessary 4WD exo-planetary rally requires.

This class has no RCS thrusters, meaning no fuel weight and therefore by far the lightest rover at 1000kgs.

[b]Rover[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/cfae7141ccbadff07d9e6c6330c942be3f8cebe6.png[/img]
A 2 ton 4WD, handling much like Earth's classic 21st century trophy trucks, rear biased 4WD and 750HP. Fitted with RCS thrusters.

[b]Mining[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/28fcf8cab4a4c6a65dee901ea795ed83128852b2.png[/img]
Re-used mining trucks once used to haul ore, these extremely heavy and cumbersome rovers require a unique and careful driving style. This rover is 6 tons, 6WD, 1900HP with no RCS thrusters.

[b]Rally[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/defb23c9a448f6cc974d344766c7f7ed3e8780d3.png[/img]
A purpose built, 1500kg, 1200HP, no costs spared 6WD exoplanetary rally rover, with RCS thrusters.

Full List
[list]
[*] 4 vehicle classes
[*] 3 planets
[*] Tensei with a single locked stage + earthquakes
[*] Rallies and Series events
[*] Time trials with a custom seed option
[*] New Bennet Engineer voice
[*] New driver and team principal portrait art (all AI now removed)
[*] Some new graphics options (screen space reflections on/off, noise on/off)
[*] Longer draw distances
[*] More accurate audio reverb/falloff at distance
[*] Donuts can be circled either clockwise or anticlockwise
[*] New music
[*] Computer reports multiple damage instances instead of listing all (we’re aware of a bug that may read this warning multiple times at once)
[*] Removed “Optimize For” fuel loads (progressive suspension mostly handles this) and matched suspension stiffness on quick setup with advanced suspension settings
[*] Improved drone spare wheel replacement
[*] Added “Repair All” on service screen
[*] Numerous menu improvements/additions
[/list]

[b]KNOWN ISSUES[/b]
[list]
[*] Expect loads of problems! This build, the classes, planets, stages have all had far less testing than Dhool + Rally class.
[*] Bennet doesn't know when he's on Tensei
[*] Mining class can crash game in replays
[*] Sometimes computer reports multiple damage instances multiple times
[*] Competetive AI times only exist for the Dhool/Rally class combo
[*] Free roam results in no sound unless you Restart
[*] Rover class RCS thrusters possibly overly sensitive
[/list]

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game - Feb 2025
notes.content:
Welcome to the first update of the year for 2025! Here's what we've been working on since the demo released at the end of last year (plus some other stuff given the demo update was a bit short!):

[h1]Multi-Planet Series[/h1]
You'll be able to run a multi-planet series (Rally class only), individual rally events using one of 4 classes, daily online leaderboards using all classes, training and free-roam. All coming for Exo Rally Early Access.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/5f0be0a7be98ea897a1cf984879fe3c1daa0f3df.jpg[/img]

[h1]We're now racing on The Moon and Tensei[/h1]
These two planets are now fully playable within individual events and the series, with any of the below classes and have setups to cater for the different gravity levels and atmospheres.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/d04437f6b6e320518ae729102a26116c6761c724.png[/img]

[h1]Rover Classes[/h1]
Early access will feature 4 classes. Here's some thumbnails for now, and we'll share full 3d renders and descriptions in the next update:


[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/638cf6e643534dc0200619f3047be599fe59f53c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/bab6fdcd43f88366342c80daf84df12440dc938f.png[/img][/url]
[b]Rally Class[/b] (the existing demo vehicle): the most powerful 6-wheel drive, a custom designed racing rover.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/25d793cec2e5609da2543430d323455a300fd128.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/a19718037325deee477f93fb7742ed6701ac0087.png[/img][/url]
[b]Rover Class[/b]: a heavy but powerful 4WD rover.


[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/cf61ef008055a6c9eacf37e6b7603e6023564dcc.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/b1dfb545340677ec8536fc87991da0301d75a3ce.png[/img][/url]
[b]UTV Class[/b]: a very small and lightweight front wheel drive vehicle.


[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/0ed6b36c6e4fedebfe2f89d58c16304548a2c855.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/79b4d91157b9e29ec8b5462faa30ec2c508d4319.png[/img][/url]
[b]Mining Class[/b]: an extremely heavy, 6WD, large mining rover.

Each class challenges your driving skills in different ways and requires unique skills to master.

[h1]New portraits and voice for NPCS[/h1]
We're almost finished replacing all the AI art and voice with human created. Here's the engineer Bennet and the Mechanic Lisa by Vladimir Matyukhin.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/6018b73fed45913c273956f2404d2ea984394aad.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/69aa85a30674185003d3c00058dfb0bc2a075187.jpg[/img]

[h1]Tensei Rework[/h1]
Given what we learned from Dhool (dust build-up isn't super fun), we've mostly removed the salt/rust aspect from Tensei. The rework now presents Tensei as an abandoned salt mining planet, with strip mined terraces used as roads, and the poor over-mined planet suffering constant earthquakes that cause temporary loss of traction. We'll likely also prototype some rock falls caused by the quakes that you'll have to dodge.

The lighting has been changed up a bit too, with pockets of light scattering across the planet, caused by extensive stellar dust and rock in the system.

Here's some making-of shots using Gaea 2.0 for height-stamp creation and Microverse/Microsplat within Unity:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/dbcd65a3f2c396ea829c814b9ae93b97d00be1f6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/e3a878d108953c4bbf2a546640ac3bd84e5b2d90.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/4925bb5585a77c113018116bf9e790d6808b67e4.png[/img]


[h1]Jimmy Hunt (Discord bot)[/h1]
Jimmy announces, in real-time, the current daily stage leaders and who's beaten who by how much:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/93fdc279c26b8f218b3a1dd6d45f19f5bd0e9638.png[/img]

[h1]List of other stuff that happened![/h1]
[list]
[*] Various supporting features/UI/art added for multi-class/setups/events
[*] Weight-based, slip-angle based drag for 'deep' or sinking ground materials like sand
[*] Slow motion replays
[*] DLSS support (WIP): We've now got DLSS and FXR(?) in which can help boost frame rates at 4k res quite substantially. 
[*] Multiple systems failure alerts instead of potentially 5-10 individual damage alerts
[*] Daily Stages - Choose other player's times to race against, receive splits vs their times
[*] Added a gyro stabilizer part - helps keep the rover level over bumps but also makes it less nimble, harder to change directions
[*] Steering wheel improvements
[*] Endless demo patches, balancing and tweaks!
[/list]

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game - July 2024
notes.content:
Welcome to the July 2024 Exo Rally update!

As we close in on the demo release, [b]we've now opened up play testing on Steam[/b], so go [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2262020/Exo_Rally_Championship/]here and request access[/url]. We hope to open up access to a few hundred new people in the coming weeks!

[h3]Industrial Planet WIP[/h3]
I've returned to this planet again this month and started adding dust drifts that form dunes and build up against structures. Also added scattered debris/concrete chunks for more interest/obstacles while racing. This planet is a research base constructed around monoliths that were originally found on the surface. An accident resulted in an explosion that scattered the power plants radioactive core across the map. Drivers will need to avoid prolonged close range exposure to the core and scattered radioactive debris. 

Still quite WIP:
[previewyoutube=FVnMxopkII8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Earth's Moon WIP[/h3]
We quite like the idea of having one or two planets from our solar system, and Earth's moon is one of them! This probably represents the most extreme low gravity rally you'll encounter in the game, and the low gravity makes for a very different experience.

[previewyoutube=t4YUfktiVVg;full][/previewyoutube]

Curious if you have any specific requests for other planets in the solar system!

[h3]Tire marks from opponents vehicles[/h3]
Now other drivers who went before you will lay tracks down in the sand/dirt, giving the rally a more populated/event-like feel, and at the same time, giving you a clue as to a nice line to take through the terrain if you haven't droned the stage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/7bf0dc8a8eae59ef650c4fbf8007dc028c928719.jpg[/img]

[h3]Steering wheel support-ish?[/h3]
We've had enough requests that we're going to 'unofficially'(?) try and support them, at least to see what people think as part of a playtest and/or the demo. The reason we're a bit cagey is the potential size of the task, with so many wheels out there, and also the fact that some wheels will be better than others for controlling the rcs thrusters (requires dpads/sticks on the wheel or another separate controller). To help, we will also be including No RCS Daily Stages specifically for wheel owners (and ofc people who love the no-rcs challenge).

Here's Rhys driving:
[previewyoutube=GiqKY62-Wj8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]New tire selection UI with full explanations[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/d923c8dadaac030ca853c7efdfc0294ae86a64f6.png[/img]

[h3]Per axis damage scaling on tires and suspension. [/h3]
Now we take more damage when landing at 'awkward angles' on our wheels. Suspension is designed mostly to cushion vertical landings and up/down movement, and landing hard on the side of your wheels will stress them more and damage them more easily.

[h3]Tire physics now allows traction at all angles of contact[/h3]
This making for better rolling (more likely to land on wheels after a crash/roll/flip) and easier to 'catch' rolls when tilting up on 3 wheels.
[previewyoutube=C9YAdEDfQys;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Rallies operate now on total points, not total time. [/h3]
Now points are earned for each stage based on your time then tallied at the end. And if you skip or extract a stage, you aren't permanently out of the rally. This has its pros and cons across the board, so curious to know what people think of this rather large diversion from classic rally rules.

There's multiple reasons for this change!:

1. Stage Hazard Rating: Stages each get rated based on things like visibility/dust/time of day, meteor shower strength, length of stage, rain, etc. 

2. Stage Skipping: Teams aren't required to drop for every stage in a rally, so you can pass or skip a stage, forfeiting any potential points. You'll often encounter scenarios where most of the field decides not to drop for a stage, because there might be an enduro length, raining, night + heavy meteor storm scenario. You can of course try to be a hero, but you'll risk the rest of your rally..!

3. Extraction system: Exoplanetary rally is incredibly hazardous and unpredictable. Drivers can extract using the dpad command system and live to fight another day, while also not being forced to limp home slowly (and boringly) on 1 or 2 wheels.

[h3]Characters added to radio/comms (WIP)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/473f7475b6e2e6ee509abc261428e3db1cfbc53f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/e3cf8be144d3880890b864eed2c98a6c50db2e2b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8a1e277e982fa83d74832b74fa4f3d08dc44e26f.png[/img]

We will go more into your team mates in future updates, but essentially, Team Lindsay, who we race for, has a Team Principal, Ed Carrington (like a CEO), Race Engineer, Bennet Clark (tactics) and Mechanic, Lisa Torres. They'll help you with priorities and goals for upcoming stages, suggest strategies, steer you away from hazard 5 stages, remind you when you forget to repair, and be in your ear as you race stages.

[h3]Removed obstacle and terrain scanners[/h3]
These systems allowed us to see through dust and darkness so we could see obstacles no matter what, which nullified the challenge and key feature of dusty environs and planets. It's quite a big change, and tough given the time we sunk into these, but we think braving the elements (or choosing not to!) with just your headlights is much more dangerous and exciting. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/a32f7796bebb434d9c5c10df972af4ced1a53b50.jpg[/img]

[h3]Dpad command system[/h3]
For resetting rover, dropship extract, repairing, etc. This enables us to use a common interface for a wide variety of in-stage actions/commands. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/f2de038269df549fb21fd08a69fb04efa09aaeee.jpg[/img]

[h3]New Dhool trees[/h3]
These are based off prehistoric Earth trees, where they were much simpler, and ofc more alien looking.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/af5482cd6621b527c3852d8b56db9a04c0a485fc.png[/img]

[h3]Drop ship pickup during stage[/h3]
You can extract any time due to damage or extreme danger situations, or automatically after stage completion (for service stages) so you can be repaired on the drop ship.

[previewyoutube=R6E0Xcl9iyg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Everything else![/h3]
- Story, dialog and next trailer work
- Weather and time now progresses from stage to stage (no longer just pure random)
- Rover engine damage smoke FX 
- Physics debugging and damage tuning
- Less damage taken from hard landings in snow and mud
- Zoomed out all replay cameras a bit so its easier to see
- Fixed bug where rock geo wasn't matching visuals perfectly
- Engine audio improvements
- Extreme Dust storm FX + high speed wind weather for Dhool
- adjusted o2 leak and tire puncture leak rates (makes more sense now you can extract from stages)
- Dhool meteor fall rates are now constant regardless of rover speed
- Tire blow out sound added
- RCS Heat generation now affected by planet temperature
- Wobbling Bobblers for antennae and other moving things on the rover
- Fixed 45 deg landings on wheels causing no damage
- More even spread of endurance/mid/sprint distances throughout a rally

[h3]Dust/element accumulation work nearly finished[/h3]
Depending on Dhool's weather, this invasive nano scale dust will either clear off (rain) or build up (dust storm) and effect almost every system on your rover

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game - March 2024
notes.content:
First Exo Rally update for 2024, here it is!

[h1]New Planet, “Tensei” [/h1]
Tensei (named “Start Planet” internally!) is essentially complete. It features mostly flat plains and rolling hills, nothing too harsh that you can smack into (just some fluffy ‘feather trees’), and both low gravity ~7m/s2 vs Earth’s 9.81 m/s2 and higher atmospheric drag (amplifies the low G feel) which generally means softer landings and lower speeds. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8ede947105a229aea868ff7805e8a9d083cb8ce9.jpg[/img]

Tensei is a salt rich environment, and drivers will want to try and steer clear of the sparkling copper-green salt fields and low hanging brine mist, else you’ll be spending a lot of time in service areas removing extreme salt build-up that can rapidly cause rust and damage half way through a rally.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/27724639486d11b09b082d1893d25c14312f614c.png[/img]

The idea for now is you’ll start your career on this planet (your team is kinda budget locked here), hoping for an invite into the wider Exo Rally Championship. So you’ll be able to get to grips with the controls on a slightly friendlier/easier planet first, and as soon as you start making meaningful placements (in the top 10 or so), you’ll be able to enter the rest of the planets in the series.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8803e92b9dde1f82c3cf48e7f5e561321ddf2fb7.png[/img]

If you're wondering what happened to the Industrial planet, featured in the November update, it's on the back burner for now. Unlike the usual terrain-based planets, this one had more challenges than anticipated, and it was dragging a bit on Rally’s schedule. My current plan is to return to it after doing a “monolith planet”, which will feature more basic shapes/geometry akin to Exo One’s. 

I’m super excited to start building the next planet, it should be a wild one! Really hoping I can finish one planet every month or two from here. 

[h1]Multi-planet Series[/h1]
You can now race in a series starting from Tensei and ending on Dhool, so the driver with the most points over the span of two rallies wins. We plan to have at least 5 when we launch into Early Access, hopefully later this year.

Rhys has been working on the interface and you can see the tabs showing the current progress up top:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/bc22913da6f98c9fa714b489d0ff6b461a79cf7c.png[/img]

[h1]Multiple Classes[/h1]
One of the best parts of most racing games is the progression from slower vehicles all the way up to the fastest, and so we’ve begun implementing new classes, so you can rise through the ranks till you reach the “Rally” class you’ve seen on the Exo Rally videos to date.

We aim to mirror Dakar's format, with highly varied classes, each which drive markedly different. Some won’t feature RCS thrusters at all, and I’m hoping to work in some lore where it’s a debate among Rally fans which is the true ‘top tier’ class, RCS equipped or not, ie “real drivers don't use cheat-thrusters!" vs "RCS thrusters are faster/more exciting/built for Exo Rally planets!".

Given we only have a tiny budget, and I recently discovered making a rover is big $$$, we’ll be using a mix of our own hand designed rovers (the 6-wheeled RCS rover you’ve seen so far) and quality 3rd party assets, which we plan to update with our own models after we leave Early Access.

Pics for these coming next update once we've done a pass over them for team livery and texturing/material work.

[h1]New! (pics below):[/h1]
[list]
[*] Planet Tensei
[*] Multi planet series
[*] First pass multiple classes
[*] Smaller 4-Wheeled UTV (no RCS, fixed setup)
[*] - Lower top speed, easier to drive, nimble
[*] Bigger, 10 ton, 6-Wheeled “Mining Truck” (no RCS, fixed setup)
[*] - Top heavy, be careful whipping the steering too much or you’ll roll easily
[*] New ending skybeams that look like search-lights, animated, criss/crossing for extra ‘flair’.
[*] First pass on NPC driver names, team names, team principals
[*] Updated leaderboards/standings displays
[*] Camera changes so driver head stays upright (gives better impression of how the rover is tilting)
[*] New fancy intro camera shots showing the dropship coming in
[*] Camera craft (like current-day camera/TV helicopters) that follow the player
[*] Watch replay footage from the camera craft’s PoV
[*] High speed wind (WIP)
[*] - Realistic directional wind for upcoming stormy planets
[*] - Fight against or use wind to your advantage, and probably wise to stay on the ground a bit more
[*] Bush/foliage impacts/drag
[*] Dense gas and water drag improvements
[/list]

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game - Dec 2023
notes.content:
We’ve got another Exo Rally update for you! Let’s get into it.

[h1]Additional Game Modes[/h1]
Exo Rally Championship has procedurally generated stages - which make drone surveys and reactionary driving very important skills - but sometimes you want to compete against other players on the same stage. We’ve added some (in-world) sponsored events where players can compete for the fastest times:

[b]Daily Sprint Stage[/b] - for those looking for a fast race (estimated 1 - 2 minute stage)

[b]Daily Endurance Stage[/b] - try and keep it together over a guaranteed long stage for the fastest time (estimated 8 - 12 minute stage)

[b]Daily Ironman Stage[/b] - players only get a single chance at this stage, so make sure to use all 3 minutes of survey drone time to plan your route!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/d76f3e44f938207938586b8c64262024e88960c7.png[/img]

A full rally event forces players to approach it differently to a single stage. The key is balancing your tires and rover’s damage over 7 stages. To that end, we’ve also added:

[b]Weekly Rally[/b] - race the same 7 stages as other players and see who can finish with the fastest time when all is said and done.

All of our new events have competitive leaderboards:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/84213dfbccf8fcb53a77aedfb9e4267a79c5ead7.png[/img]

[h1]Damage[/h1]
We’re always trying to balance rover damage so it feels more predictable, and we’ve taken another step in this direction. A single impact can mean death for your driver (if it’s hard enough of course), but avoid that and damage is sure to accumulate over time. During a Rally, you will be forced to make some hard choices on which parts to repair and which you think you can deal with.

We’ve also added breakable headlights - good luck driving through a thick fog in the dead of night without them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/6b3ef5cd9a10822562b2b9948dfe9594b4ab8638.png[/img]

[h1]What happened to muh Tires![/h1]
We’ve added tire punctures and tire pressure. Hit a sharp rock too hard and you might get a tire puncture, the pressure draining slowly over time. Eventually your tire may detach completely, leaving you driving on a wheel rim only!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/36f07df8029f5466d1156d780b6bbdc35e991a8f.png[/img]

[h1]Pitch Ladder[/h1]
In Exo Rally you’ll flip your car a lot. Seriously. It’s a very important thing to know when you’re upside down, as is just how steep the hill you’re trying to climb might be, so we’ve added a pitch ladder to the HUD:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8f8a7906a8cea24908733d9f98e9e03d1ce83fc4.png[/img]

[h1]Stage Seeds[/h1]
We talked a bit about our procedural stages above, but another thing to mention is we’ve refined how one of the seed characters work and given players complete control over the length of the stage. If you like a certain stage but think  it’s too short, all you need to do is change one character in the seed and you’ll get a much longer version (and vice versa)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/4cb81e0079acfb20642dba6cd89b156f63e05439.png[/img]

We’re also now storing your most recent and your most played seeds so you’ll never forget your favourite stages.

notes.title: Exo Rally, State of the Game - Nov 2023
notes.content:
Welcome to the November Exo Rally Championship update!

This month we’ve been working on a new planet and a more feature rich, more punishing damage system. There’s lots more damage types, like bent RCS thrusters/locked or destroyed brakes/snapped off suspension arms (you're really in trouble...) and even destroying your exterior camera link:

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/LnyfGx1YNF4

[previewyoutube=Y-x3dWrT0sY;full][previewyoutube=yVxHAlW-moE;full][/previewyoutube][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Industrial Planet[/h2]
While the majority of planets in Exo Rally will likely be natural, uninhabited worlds, the handful of monoliths scattered on Dhool made us feel that there was some serious fun to be had riding man-made walls and structures.

Given how much verticality there is on this planet, objects to avoid, walls to ride, etc, we’re also using it as a test-case for quite low (almost .5 earth) gravity and high (3x?) atmospheric drag. So you’ll float a bit more and not reach such deadly falling velocities.

The industrial planet will be the most built up surface we will race on, featuring almost purely man made buildings, walls, streets, tunnels, bridges and so on. It should help inform us of what the polar opposite of a natural world is like, and what challenges lie here for development going forward. Basically it's serving as a prototype for all levels that feature any artificial driving surfaces, and challenging our existing terrain-only physics at the same time!

Right now we’re prototyping various surface and structure types and seeing what stages are like, and once we’ve locked down the geometry we will proceed with detailing it, adding visuals etc.

Here’s a peek:

[previewyoutube=nEvv6BvsrKo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]RCS Thruster Heat[/h2]
RCS thrusters now generate heat when you use them - if you push them too hard and they overheat, you can't use them until they've cooled back down. Driving at high speed or in the rain will help with cooling! We’re also highly considering an override for overheating, in the same vein as Mechwarrior. So if you override and keep overheating, you’ll suffer things like thrusters melting, fuel exploding and so on.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/QY8YJOq.png[/img]

[h2]Tire Degradation and Selection[/h2]
Expect to start losing grip as your tire tread wears down (especially during a rally where you have a limited tire allocation). Before the start of a rally, you’ll now choose 2 sets (with spares) based on the lengths of upcoming stages, their surface types and weather conditions. Depending on how many tires or wheels you shred or rip off during the rally, you’ll find yourself swapping tires in and out based on their wear, their position on the rover, whether it’s a spare, etc.

Tire Set Selection
[img]https://i.imgur.com/BczZfxQ.png[/img]

Changing Tires Mid Rally
[img]https://i.imgur.com/HxMIa0k.png[/img]

When you reach a certain level of tire slip (wheel spin), the HUD will also alert you by flashing the wheel icons.

On that note, both offroad and slick tires now have a choice between soft/hard compounds, and traction in general has been slightly increased.

[h2]Power Stages[/h2]
The final stage in a rally is now a power stage, which is a repeat of the shortest of the previous stages and awards extra points for the top 5 finishers. Dropped the ball and are coming in way down the order? Save your tires for the power stage and get yourself some much needed points. Fighting for first place but have already pushed your tires to the limit? Take it easy on the power stage - securing first place is more important. 

[h2]Meteor Showers[/h2]
Meteor showers are much deadlier now, as they throw out shrapnel upon landing. The high speed shrapnel pierces your rover like bullets that can damage important components. Avoidance is key!

Meteors now have the following characteristics - direct hits are usually fatal, near misses throw the rover about and unsettle you, especially if you’re airborne, and shrapnel can rip through your systems if you’re too close to impacts.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/JMysePN.jpg[/img]

[h2]Skid Plate Scraping & Sparks[/h2]
Rover skid plate/floor collisions and scraping is much improved, allowing you to setup a much lower rover (we're including some presets if you want to test them out). The thick floor plate features some damage impact reduction, but eventually if you scrape along too much you’ll wear through it and start taking more serious damage.

[previewyoutube=rDJ3P-KVSOI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Wet Rain[/h2]
Watch it reflect in satisfying wayz in the rain plz!:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/GvsULPx.png[/img]

[h2]And More[/h2]
There are lots more improvements/fixes too, like to the UI and Dhool’s terrain features. Overall we're hoping rallies give a real sense of impending doom as you manage rover repairs and tires to hopefully get you to the end.

notes.title: Exo Rally Championship - State of the Game
notes.content:
October 2023

Hi all, it’s been a few months since we announced the game, which we’re calling “The final frontier of racing - remote, unexplored, extreme exoplanetary rally!” If you didn’t catch that first post, here’s an overview of the game: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2262020/view/3671043467005543838?snr=1_5_9_

So here’s an update on where we’re at, approximately 1.5 years into development:

Vertical slice is in/working well - you can now run a single 6 stage rally on one planet, complete with service stages, drone recce/prerunning, surface types, damage, repairing, rover tuning, first pass AI opponents and so on. You can enter the rally, look at the upcoming stage, how long it is, what surfaces and terrain to expect, and send out a drone to survey what you’ll be driving through. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/0263773f9eccd179821ea21ba0acf7e1198a027e.jpg[/img]

You can then choose how much fuel to take, what tires (off-road or slick for rock), and setup/tune your rover. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/8eee7720c3918db790fecb6740a5953dd55ad796.jpg[/img]

After driving 2 stages you’re back into your dropship where you can make repairs or alter your tuning based on the next 2 stages. You can watch all the action from each stage via Instant Replay from a variety of angles, and if you complete the next 4 stages from there, your time will be tallied against the AI to determine your final placing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/a9b2a3af44275689d8e14fd398e80e4289a9ef73.jpg[/img]

From here, the biggest thing we need to add will be multiple, quite varied planet types, so you can race a full championship across 5-6+ planets! The first planet we have is Dhool, which is special due to its unceasing meteor falls, which create an ever changing series of deadly obstacles to dodge around, and which also cause the atmosphere to be filled with an incredibly fine dust that gets everywhere, and clogs everything if you aren’t careful. It’s also home to some highly radioactive lakes you’ll need to be very careful around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/a5eaa4cbda5900df18ec584d319781a8e4d77674.jpg[/img]

Most recently we’ve been focused on tuning and damage, and I’ve begun prototyping the next (very very different) planet, which will represent the opposite end of the spectrum for what kinds of planets you’ll encounter in Exo Rally Championship.

Tuning is available prior to starting a rally, and during service stages, and allows players to adjust everything from tire choice to suspension stiffness to toe-in and bump/rebound damper settings. If you’re used to setting up cars in existing racing sims you’ll feel right at home here. We’ve also got a streamlined, ‘easy mode’ setup system, where you can either load complete setups (for example, stiffer/low riding/responsive or softer/tall suspension setups) or provide top-level setup choices like ride height and suspension stiffness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/c49467c5c1797aa555f1875bd8c2288d5766c56b.jpg[/img]

Damage is a huge part of Exo Rally, and we’re pouring in lots of time to make sure you feel the impact these toxic, treacherous planets have on every part of your rover. We’re modelling everything from standard engine damage all the way up to how radioactive nano dust gets in and impacts your brake strength and radiator efficiency. So make sure you wash your rover between stages! Just a small number of parts that can be damaged/break:
[list]
[*] Engine
[*] Tires and Wheels
[*] Suspension
[*] Suspension arms
[*] RCS Thrusters
[*] RCS Fuel Tank
[*] Brakes
[*] Steering
[*] O2 leaks and Cabin Integrity
[*] Headlights
[*] And much more!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238168/88d3094b88b1b6cf3b0a9d2f5fd1668b9823aa9d.jpg[/img]

We’ll be polishing up this current build and sharing it soon with our small group of private testers. If you’d like to be considered for the next group of testers please come join us in the Discord and we’ll let you know!

Discord: https://discord.gg/75wYhXzHP3


Would love to hear any feedback or ideas you have, or what you’d like to see in Exo Rally, so feel free to join us on Discord or leave a comment here.

You can also follow us on Twitter here:
https://twitter.com/JayWeston

https://twitter.com/biscuitsmitten

https://twitter.com/RhysLindsay
